key_risks: 10-year Treasury yields continuing to climb past 5.18%, triggering broader equity multiple compression.
10yr yields could overshoot further if upcoming CPI (10/14) or PCE (9/30) data show inflation reaccelerating, given already-hawkish Fed language.
An oil supply shock extending Brent's rise despite the EIA path.
Brent crude oil spot prices ($114.89) failing to normalize toward the $90/bbl EIA expectation, reigniting headline inflation pressures.
Consumer fatigue: saving rate 3%, sentiment 51.7, decelerating retail sales.
Escalation of international trade disputes following USTR hearings and retaliatory tariffs.
Higher-for-longer long-term bond yields (10y at 5.18%) triggering broader equity valuation de-rating and slowing housing activity.
October FOMC hike with a hawkish guide pushing the 10-year above 5.3%.
Oil prices remain well above EIA's projected average; a failure to retrace would keep inflation expectations elevated and pressure the Fed to stay restrictive longer.
Persistent elevated oil prices (Brent at $114.89) reigniting headline inflation and forcing the Fed beyond its 4.1% target rate projection.
Personal savings rate at 3.0% combined with 7.03% mortgage rates curtailing consumer discretionary spending.

Stale/unusual data flags (copper, gasoline, food index, JOLTS) create risk that the growth/inflation picture shifts materially once fresh prints arrive (JOLTS 9/29, Employment Situation 10/2, CPI 10/14).
Tight HY spreads (2.80) and a low VIX leave little cushion for a risk-off shock.
Trade-policy frictions (Canada retaliation, Section 301 pharma probe, sugar TRQs) are early-stage and could escalate into sector-specific shocks not yet reflected in factor sensitivities.
